name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPA-16M 'Mudwork'
description:
The KPA-16M is an environmental hardening package applied to the KPA-16 platform — not a new rifle so much as a KPA-16 that has been built from the ground up to tolerate the conditions that destroy ordinary KPA-16s. The barrel is coated in Slagworks' Ferrolock nitride treatment, which provides corrosion resistance that outlasts chrome lining in salt and industrial-chemical environments. The lower receiver is sealed at the buffer tube interface, the trigger group cavity, and the mag well with low-durometer gaskets that exclude particulate without significantly affecting the cycling feel. The handguard is a reinforced polymer unit with sealed rail sections that prevent grit ingress around the attachment points. Internally, the bolt carrier group runs tighter tolerances with a specialized lubricant coating that doesn't require re-application as frequently as standard mil-spec grease. The result is a rifle that tolerates neglect, chemical exposure, and prolonged operation in GLMZ's most hostile environments without the reliability degradation that afflicts standard configurations.

The KPA-16M was not developed for military or law enforcement customers — it was developed because Slagworks Industrial's own facility security personnel were destroying KPA-16s at an accelerated rate in the chemical processing and heavy industrial zones of the GLMZ's manufacturing belt. Those environments — caustic chemical exposure, metal particulate in the air, standing water on every surface — eat firearms faster than combat does, and the standard KPA-16 wasn't surviving routine deployment cycles. The M-model solved the problem internally before Kang-Petrov released it commercially, which is why it carries Slagworks' implicit endorsement in a way that few KP civilian products do.

Operators who carry the KPA-16M in the manufacturing belt have a saying: 'The M stands for it still works.' That's reductive — the M-model is genuinely a better-engineered product than the base KPA-16 in specific conditions — but it captures something true about why people buy it. The finish is uglier than the standard model (the nitride coating is matte and slightly uneven), the gaskets add a few hundred grams, and the sealed rail sections require a specific tool to open cleanly. None of that matters when your operating environment is a Slagworks acid-recovery facility and your colleagues have gone through three standard rifles in a year.
specifications:
caliber: 5.56mm Combat Standard
effective_range: 400m
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 30 rounds
weight: 3.4 kg
tactical_use: The KPA-16M operates identically to the standard KPA-16 in tactical application but is specifically optimized for sustained deployment in chemically aggressive, high-particulate, or waterlogged environments. The extended lubrication interval — roughly three times the standard KPA-16's recommended cleaning cycle — is its primary operational advantage in field conditions where maintenance is opportunistic rather than scheduled. Operators running it in manufacturing-belt environments typically pair it with sealed optics and a sling rated for chemical exposure.
cultural_context: The KPA-16M is a working-environment rifle. It doesn't carry tactical cachet in the fixer community — it's not a fighting rifle, it's a conditions rifle — but in the manufacturing belt and industrial zones of the GLMZ, it's the standard by which other rifles are judged. Facility security personnel who carry it tend to be unimpressed by operators who obsess over exotic platforms. They've learned to value the thing that works when the environment is trying to kill the weapon.
story_hooks: A KPA-16M recovered from an abandoned Slagworks acid-recovery facility shows evidence of having been fired recently — the nitride coating is still in excellent condition despite the environment, but the magazine was empty and there are impact marks on the receiver consistent with a struggle. The facility was supposedly decommissioned two years ago.

A shipment of KPA-16M environmental hardening kits — the gaskets, nitride-coated components, and sealed handguards sold as an aftermarket upgrade package — was intercepted at a GLMZ internal transit checkpoint. The destination was not a manufacturing facility or security contractor; it was a residential address in an Excluded zone, which means either a very well-prepared individual or a community that is preparing for something.
